clinician.trajectory_summary: A 40-year-old female presented with an 18-month history of an intermittently painful medial right forearm mass, notably tender and firm in relation to menstruation. Initial radiographs were normal. MRI revealed a 2.2 x 2.1 x 3.0 cm oval intramuscular mass in the anterior proximal forearm with heterogeneous T2 signal and cystic changes. Ultrasound showed a circumscribed hypoechoic mass with internal doppler flow. An ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy was performed but was nondiagnostic. Subsequently, an open biopsy with frozen section diagnosis was performed, confirming endometriosis.
